tagline: Across southern Vermont on General Stark's road home.
intro: Route 9 comes over the Connecticut River from New Hampshire on a through arch bridge into Brattleboro, then heads west up Whetstone Brook, past Marlboro and over Hogback Mountain, and down Beaver Brook into Wilmington. It follows the Deerfield River up to Searsburg, tops the Green Mountains at Big Pond in Woodford, and comes down City Stream and the Walloomsac River into Bennington.

This is the way General John Stark's army went home to New Hampshire after the Battle of Bennington in 1777. The road is named for his wife Molly, who had figured in his battle cry: the enemy would be theirs, or that night Molly Stark would sleep a widow.

moments.title: Hogback Mountain
moments.text: The mountain stands just north of the highway, and its overlook, known as the 100-mile view, takes in Vermont, New Hampshire and Massachusetts.

moments.title: Wilmington
moments.text: Downtown, near the Deerfield River, Molly Stark herself stands in statue form, holding a child and a musket.

moments.title: Bennington Battle Monument
moments.text: A 306-foot stone obelisk marks the Battle of Bennington, which was actually fought over the line in New York.

sources.label: Brattleboro Area Chamber of Commerce, Route 9, The Molly Stark Byway
